disfluency_verdict.decision: Fold into the LLM polishing pass
disfluency_verdict.reasoning: Specialized disfluency-removal models (DisfluencyFixer, DISCO) are research-grade and primarily EN/HI/DE/FR — Spanish coverage is sparse. Tier-B LLMs (Gemma 4 26B MoE, Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B) handle disfluency removal extremely well as part of an instruction-following pass. Adding a separate component means another model loaded, another VRAM slot, another point of failure, and worse multilingual coverage than the LLM you already run. This holds regardless of which transcribe/translate front-end eventually feeds it.
disfluency_verdict.prompt:
Clean up this transcript:
- Remove filler words (um, uh, eh, este, like, you know)
- Remove false starts and self-corrections, keep the corrected version
- Tighten conciseness without losing meaning or voice
- Preserve technical terms and proper nouns exactly
- Keep the output in [Spanish/English] — do not translate

{transcript}

top_picks.why: Best small agentic model on this hardware as of mid-November 2026 — and still the incumbent. Hybrid DeltaNet + sparse MoE, 262k native ctx, 201 languages, Apache 2.0. No 4B-class challenger has shipped.

99 t/s, full 256k context, Google-grade multilingual including Catalan. Tie with Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B persists through eleven consecutive runs — keep Gemma as default on Catalan track record; switch to Qwen 3.6 if you need pure Apache 2.0. Both MoE leaders beat every new entrant surveyed to date on verified/fitting speed, including a now-confirmed-shipped Mistral Large 4, Muse Spark Open, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt, Kimi K3.1 Pro, and Ripple-65B Preview.

BFCL leader at 75.7%. ~10 t/s with mild CPU spill — reserve for batch quality runs where correctness > latency. Still beats every other Tier C entrant evaluated to date on verified speed, including this window's two new entrants.
